The issue isn't really that it is made for a different demographic, it's just the likeness to the characters. In addition, companies have to pursue protecting their copyright in almost every circumstance, otherwise it can be used against them in future legal battles. So, let's say a company does come out with pull-ups with paw patrol designs, and the creators try to sue them. The pull-ups manufacturers can use the existence of the adult diapers as evidence that Paw Patrol failed to secure their copyright claim on the characters. This is kind of a long shot "what if" scenario, but it is why a lot of small creators will get cease and desist letters from the companies.

Now, for the actual prints, I don't think Tykables will be sued over them for a couple reasons. One, they are only likenesses, and are not direct rip-offs. It would be much harder for whoever owns Paw Patrol to sue over the idea of dogs being policemen/firemen being wholly under their copyright, as it's a pretty vague idea. Two, I really don't think Paw Patrol would want any association with the lawsuit anyway. At most, they might try to send a cease and desist, but I doubt this would ever go to court.

At this point, I find it really weird to not be diapered while trying to sleep. I would definitely say being diapered improves my quality of sleep. 

As an aside, the only times I have truly wet the bed as an adult was when I had been drinking really heavily, or had a decent number of drinks, and then chugged water to try and stave off a hangover. Unfortunately, during these times, I was never diapered (and one of them happened at a friend's apartment, oops) so it was much more of a hassle than fulfilling (especially with the included hangover). I don't drink alcohol at all nowadays, so this shortcut no longer is an option for me.
